title: "Day 21: Model comparison for logistic regression"

```{r}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(ggformula)
library(broom)
library(patchwork)
library(here)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
source("notes-helpers.R")

news <- read.csv(here("data", "fake_news_bayesrules.csv"))

news_mod <- glm(type_num ~ title_words + title_has_excl + title_caps_percent,
                data = news, family = "binomial")
news_mod2 <- glm(type_num ~ title_words + title_has_excl * title_caps_percent,
                 data = news, family = "binomial")
reduced_model <- glm(type_num ~ title_words + title_caps_percent,
                     data = news, family = "binomial")
null_model <- glm(type_num ~ 1, data = news, family = "binomial")

f2 <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)
f3 <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)
```

Last time we learned how to do inference for **one** coefficient (Wald test and CI) and how to check conditions. Today we compare **models**:

1.  Do we need an interaction term?
2.  The **likelihood ratio test** (LRT): the logistic version of the extra sums of squares $F$-test
3.  AIC and BIC for logistic regression

## The model from last time

```{r}
kable_coef(news_mod, terms = c("Intercept", "title_words", "title_has_exclTRUE", "title_caps_percent"))
```

**Question:** is the association between `title_caps_percent` and the odds of being fake news *different* for titles with and without an exclamation point? That is, do we need an **interaction** between `title_has_excl` and `title_caps_percent`?


```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 2.5
news_agg <- news |>
  mutate(tcp_bin = cut(title_caps_percent, c(-Inf, 0, 10, Inf))) |>
  group_by(tcp_bin, title_has_excl) |>
  summarize(mean_x = mean(title_caps_percent), n = n(), n_fake = sum(type_num),
            emp_logit = log((n_fake + 0.5) / (n - n_fake + 0.5)), .groups = "drop")

p1 <- gf_boxplot(type ~ title_caps_percent, color = ~title_has_excl, fill = ~title_has_excl, data = news, height = .25, width = 1, alpha = .5) + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") + 
  scale_color_viridis_d(end = .75, option = "plasma") + 
  scale_fill_viridis_d(end = .75, option = "plasma") 

p2 <- gf_point(emp_logit ~ mean_x, color = ~title_has_excl, data = news_agg) |>
  gf_smooth(method = "lm") + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") + 
  scale_color_viridis_d(end = .75, option = "plasma") 

p1 + p2 
```



## The model with an interaction

$$\text{logit}(\pi_i) = \beta_0 + \beta_1\, \text{words}_i + \beta_2\, \text{excl}_i + \beta_3\, \text{caps}_i + \beta_4\, (\text{excl}_i \times \text{caps}_i)$$

```{r}
kable_coef(news_mod2, terms = c("Intercept", "title_words", "title_has_exclTRUE", "title_caps_percent",
                                "title_has_exclTRUE:title_caps_percent"))
```

## The likelihood ratio test (LRT)

In linear regression we compared nested models with the ______________________________ $F$-test. For logistic regression we use a **likelihood ratio test**.

::: callout-note
## Deviance

The **deviance** of a model is $-2 \log L$, where $L$ is the maximized likelihood. Like SSE in OLS, a smaller deviance means a ______________ fit. A bigger model always has a deviance that is the same or ______________.

:::

::: callout-note
## Likelihood Ratio Test

**Hypotheses:** $H_0$: ______________________________ vs. $H_a$: at least one of these $\beta$'s $\ne 0$

**Test statistic:** $\Lambda = \text{Dev(reduced)} - \text{Dev(full)}$

**Reference distribution:** $\chi^2$ with $df =$ ______________________________

**p-value:** the area ______________ $\Lambda$ (upper tail)

:::

In R, give the **reduced** model first:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
anova(reduced_model, full_model, test = "LRT")
```

| Resid DF | Resid Dev | Df | Deviance | Pr(\>Chi) |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| $n -$ (p+1 in reduced) | Dev(reduced) | | | |
| $n -$ (p+1 in full) | Dev(full) | # extra coefs | $\Lambda$ | p-value |

## $z$-test vs. LRT

For one coefficient, $H_0: \beta_i = 0$:

-   In OLS, the $t$-test and $F$-test give *exactly* the same p-value.
-   In logistic regression the $z$-test (Wald) and the LRT are ______________ equivalent. Hopefully they are close. If not, the ______________ is usually more accurate.

```{r}
lrt_p <- function(term) {
  reduced <- update(news_mod, as.formula(paste(". ~ . -", term)))
  anova(reduced, news_mod, test = "LRT")[2, "Pr(>Chi)"]
}

terms <- c("title_words", "title_has_excl", "title_caps_percent")
tibble(term = terms,
       `z-test p-value` = summary(news_mod)$coefficients[-1, "Pr(>|z|)"],
       `LRT p-value` = map_dbl(terms, lrt_p)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)
```

The LRT can also test **several coefficients at once**, which the $z$-test cannot.

## AIC and BIC for logistic regression

$$AIC = -2\log(L) + 2k \qquad\qquad BIC = -2\log(L) + \log(n) \cdot k$$

where $L$ is the maximized likelihood and $k$ is the number of coefficients (including the intercept). For binary logistic regression, $-2\log(L)$ is the ______________. Smaller is better, and both can compare nested **or** non-nested models.

```{r}
data.frame(AIC(reduced_model, news_mod, news_mod2),
           BIC = BIC(reduced_model, news_mod, news_mod2)$BIC) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

**Q6.** Which model do AIC and BIC prefer? Do they agree with the LRTs?

\vspace{.75in}

## Summary

| To compare... | Use | 
|:--|:-------------|
| one coefficient to 0 | |
| several coefficients to 0, nested models | |
| non-nested models, or many models | |

-   Deviance is $-2\log L$. It plays the role of ______ in OLS.
-   We use deviance to compare models

## R function reference

| Function | Purpose |
|:--|:--|
| `anova(reduced, full, test = "LRT")` | Likelihood ratio test for nested models |
| `deviance(model)` | Deviance ($-2\log L$) of a model |
| `pchisq(x, df)` | $\chi^2$ probability; use `1 - pchisq()` for a p-value |
| `update(model, . ~ . - term)` | Refit a model without one term |
| `AIC(m1, m2, ...)`, `BIC(m1, m2, ...)` | Information criteria for one or more models |
